content.title: About
content.content: Potato is a root vegetable cultivated worldwide. Fresh home fries are diced or sliced pieces of potato pan‑fried until golden. They have a mild, slightly sweet flavor, a crisp exterior and a tender interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes were introduced to Europe from South America in the 16th century.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties differing in color, shape, and taste.
Home fries are often made from young potatoes, which retain more nutrients.
Potato starch is used in the food industry as a thickener and for making chips.
In Russia, fried potatoes are traditionally served with dill, sour cream, or tartar sauce.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports heart function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in fat when prepared properly
items.content: When pan‑fried with a modest amount of oil, home fries remain relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: High carbohydrate content
items.content: Large portions can raise blood sugar levels, which is important for people with diabetes.

items.title: Acrylamide formation at high heat
items.content: Over‑heating can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

items.title: Rare potato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Salt content when seasoned
items.content: Excessive salt can contribute to elevated blood pressure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Home fries can be served as a side dish with meat, fish or vegetables, added to salads, soups, or enjoyed as a snack. For a healthier version, fry in olive or sunflower oil and season with fresh herbs, garlic, and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh potatoes in a cool, dark, dry place away from direct sunlight. Cooked home fries should be cooled and kept in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 2‑3 days.
